free_tier.stated: No published free tier: USD 299 per Runner per month, with a Trial Period of unspecified length stated in the cloud terms of service and no fee during it; the checkout email field is the only published gate.
free_tier.notes: The price page states one paid tier and no free minutes, credit or trial length; the terms define a Trial Period with no fee and automatic conversion to the paid monthly subscription, but give no number of days.

per_object_cap.stated: 1 GiB per file uploaded through sim-remote, from the sessions reference; the runner unit is a Mac with simulators, not an object store
per_object_cap.notes: The 1 GiB limit applies to every file sim-remote uploads, such as an app bundle.

retention.stated: Nothing survives a session: on release or logout the session credentials are revoked, connections closed, simulators erased and the session volume rebuilt from a clean image; operational logs are kept 14 days.

egress.terms: unverified: no per-GB egress price or quota is published; the runner price is flat and a forward tunnel reaches only the servers of the session itself

interface_detail: An authenticated API reached through the open-source sim-remote CLI: sim-remote simctl is a drop-in for xcrun simctl, with a web UI showing live previews; Appium, Maestro and Argent E2E drive the simulators.
tooling: sim-remote CLI on macOS, Linux or a cloud sandbox, the Argent toolkit and its MCP server, and a web UI; test suites use Appium, Maestro or Argent E2E.
chaining: A Linux CI job or coding agent reserves a hosted Mac for iOS simulator work without a macOS runner; because session data is erased on release, test artifacts must be written to a separate storage record.

limits.value: Up to 6 iOS simulators running in parallel per Runner, each Mac reserved for one project and never shared with other customers
idle release after 900 seconds (15 minutes) without a sim-remote command; the server has its own idle limit of 16 minutes
a session holds one machine for at most 24 hours, enforced by the server
1 GiB for each file uploaded by sim-remote
self-serve checkout covers up to 4 Runners; a bigger fleet requires sales contact

limits_note: Connection details arrive within 2 business days of order; a session token lasts 24 hours and waiting for a free machine defaults to 1800 seconds with a 3600-second server cap.
binding_note: The price is flat and the published parallelism is six simulators, so the constraint that cuts a job first is the 900-second idle release and the 24-hour cap on holding one machine.

identity_cost.detail: An API key is issued to the user on request and sent directly; the order form asks for a checkout email and payment is completed through a payment processor. The sign-up page itself was not entered, so any further identity fields are unverified: behind a sign-up.

reliability_note: A machine is released after 15 minutes idle and at most 24 hours held; simulators and session state are erased on release, and the service depends on a third-party macOS infrastructure supplier.
confidence_note: The price, parallelism, checkout email and self-serve cap come from the provider pricing page read 2026-11-24; the idle and lifetime caps come from the cloud sessions reference, and the identity and egress gates were read but not entered.
